title: Loop
rule: The last panel leads back into the first: he returns to the desk, reads the memo and sets off again, so the page reads round forever.
declares: E0 repeated after E5 (the loop seam)
made: FORAGED: three Daumier lithographs (CC0, Rijksmuseum via Commons; licence read from the Commons API extmetadata 2026-11-17), 1280 px renders, levelled once per print (red-filter luminance to drop the newsprint foxing, black/white points, a 0.8 px softening of the newsprint speckle; no threshold or posterize)

HANDMADE cuts: hand-placed scissor polygons for the agent's head and body (cut apart at the collar so the head tilts: down to the memo, up to the clock), the woman, the window and the door; set pieces (desk, counter, cupboard and leaf, clock ring, dial and case, pencil) cut out of the prints' own crayon tone; every piece glued with a narrow paper rim and cast shadow on the LoC 1934 sheet
the ANRC 1922 key cutout (99-ways-template piece) glued in the cupboard, warmed to brass, with a SERVICE tag slip

the loop: eight panels in a ring round the memo, read clockwise from the top left; every gutter connector a heavy pen arrow (11 px line, 24 px head, about 94 px long, reaching into both panels, on a paper halo) like the seam arrow from P8 up into P1; the bottom row's arrows point right to left (P5 -> P6 -> P7); small pasted paper discs numbered 1-8 at each panel's top-left corner; a ring of arrows and 'round and round' round the central memo

P7: a HANDMADE pencil (shaft cut from the window's pale paper warmed to yellow, a ferrule from the carriage wall's tone, a sharpened cone and a lead point from the tunnel's black) held up from his waistcoat, its point touching his chin; no grafted hands
pen-hand clock numerals and hands at 4:10, captions, the four canon lines in cut-paper balloons, the TICKET OFFICE and SERVICE slips; folio by pen99.folio

events.E0: P1 at his desk, the memo again ('4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'), head bent to it; P2 he sets off for the key; the memo also sits large at the centre of the ring
events.E1: P3 the woman behind the TICKET OFFICE window; question balloon
events.E2: P4 head tilted up to the clock at 4:10; answer balloon
events.E3: P5 she turns away from the window; thanks balloon
events.E4: P6 the cupboard open, the key on its hook
events.E5: P7 pencil point at his chin, the forgetting line; the key still in the cupboard, the SERVICE door shut
events.loop seam (declared): P8 he walks back to his desk; the arrow runs from P8 up into P1, where he reads the memo and sets off again

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: the loop seam: in P8 he walks back to the desk (three positions), the heavy seam arrow appears from P8 into P1, and in P1 his head bends to the memo again
beat_frames: b01: P8 he turns back, P1 head level, no seam arrow
b02: P8 halfway to the desk
b04: the seam arrow P8 -> P1 is drawn
b05: P1 his head bends to the memo

self_check.layout: 3x3 ring, centre cell the memo; reading clockwise from top left; P8 at middle left leads up into P1
self_check.check: A reader can continue from the last panel straight into the first. -> P8's caption 'And back he goes to his desk...' and the heavy seam arrow lead into P1's 'The memo again...'; the numbers 1-8 and the heavy gutter arrows fix the bottom row as 5 (thanks) -> 6 (cupboard) -> 7 (forgetting)
self_check.evidence: measured (size, pixel checks named in the repair) and judged from the full-size page by the repair maker; a fresh blind reading of the repair is pending

weaknesses: the agent is a Daumier bourgeois in a top hat and tail-coat (waistcoat kept, shirt-sleeves not); the hat indoors is the price of a print whose figure stands whole
the agent is the same cut-out in every panel (only head tilt, flip and position change): his walk is a glide, not a stride
the panel grounds are one stretched patch of the stairwell wall and floor, softened to keep the JPEG under 1.2 MB; they read as tone, not as a station office
the clock is built (tone ring, pale dial, pen hands) rather than found: no Daumier clock was in the three prints
the pencil in P7 has no hand holding it (the Daumier body's arms hang at his sides); it reads as a pencil raised to the chin, held from below the frame of the waistcoat
the empty white hook above the key was deleted; the key hangs in the cupboard without a drawn hook, though the P6 caption says 'on its hook'

changed: every gutter arrow redrawn as a heavy arrow (same weight as the seam arrow), about 94 px long, on a paper halo; the bottom row's three arrows point right to left
ordinal discs 1-8 at each panel's top-left corner
P7: the Daumier clasped-hands piece removed from his chest; a pale pencil cut set so its point touches his chin
the stray empty white hook above the key deleted (P6, P7)
the wall ground softened 2.4 -> 3.2 px to stay under 1.2 MB after the additions
repairs.pass_test: a fresh blind reader lists the bottom row as thanks, cupboard, forgetting, and names the pencil at his chin
